conclusionLimit: A static literal clock improved the already stripped diagnostic, but replacing Live Timer with native HH:mm in the full widget showed no perceived loading improvement. The clock replacement is not an established fix and will not be promoted. Minimal Home improved further, supporting isolation of additional Home content/evaluation. No test identifies every remaining cost or establishes quantitative latency. Removing the 200 progress drawings from the full widget did not produce a noticeable improvement; this does not prove zero cost or rule out interactions. Removing another 137 weather-icon nodes also did not improve perceived waiting. These later tests used the full live-data baseline, whereas fast Minimal uses stripped sources. A native HH:mm vs Live Timer comparison cannot rule out the cost of displaying an active clock because both variants display time. Restoring only the approved live clock to Minimal kept the transition fast. Preserve the approved clock; this does not rule out interactions with other Home content. Four Home event fields on the fast clock baseline remained relatively fast with a possible slight slowdown. This does not reproduce the full-Home delay. Restoring the 13 greeting/date/day-progress text layers also produced no perceived slowdown. These source/display groups remain possible interaction partners, not established causes. Restoring the remaining native Home text and three real shared sources produced only a very slight perceived slowdown. Next isolate the approved static backdrop on this same live-text baseline. Restoring the original backdrop caused another small perceived slowdown. This implicates its complete image path or interactions, but does not separate delivery from decoding/rendering. An embedded-data-URL copy is a compatibility-first experiment, not yet a performance fix. User confirms the embedded backdrop renders normally and reports no significant speed improvement. This weakens a dominant backdrop-download explanation, but does not measure cache behavior or prove zero network cost. Retain the same tested embedded backdrop in the next graphics add-back to avoid changing two groups at once.
